topic: AIPMM Certified Product Manager (CPM) exam preparation - the AIPMM credential covering the front end of the product life cycle from idea to launch: market research, product strategy and business planning, product definition, roadmapping, and go-to-market, grounded in the AIPMM ProdBOK and Seven-Phase Product Life Cycle
exam_format: Approximately a 2-hour, ~120-question, proctored, closed-book multiple-choice exam. The exam voucher is purchased from AIPMM (a division of Prodex, Inc.) and can be taken exam-only or bundled with an Authorized Training Partner course (e.g. Productside). AIPMM does NOT publicly publish the passing score or official per-domain percentage weightings, so the domain weights in this course are editorial estimates that reflect the emphasis of the AIPMM ProdBOK and Seven-Phase Product Life Cycle, not AIPMM's official figures. Exam pricing varies by training partner and region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current AIPMM pricing.
question_types: multiple choice, single answer, exactly 4 options; scenario- and definition-based questions drawn from the AIPMM ProdBOK terminology and framework
audience: Product managers, associate/aspiring PMs, product owners, and cross-functional leads (engineering, marketing, UX) who want a vendor-neutral, globally recognized product management credential. Candidates typically have 1-3 years of product or adjacent experience. A strong foundation before the more digital- and delivery-focused AIPMM CDPM, and a complement to the technical certifications in this catalog for learners moving into AI/tech product roles.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Product Management Foundations and the ProdBOK Life Cycle
domains.notes: The AIPMM Product Body of Knowledge (ProdBOK) as the exam's backbone: the role and responsibilities of the product manager vs product owner vs product marketing manager, the vocabulary the exam tests, and the Seven-Phase Product Life Cycle (conceive, plan, develop, qualify, launch, maximize, retire). Phase-gate / stage-gate process modeling and how gate decisions are made. Inbound vs outbound activities and where the PM 'go-to' function coordinates internal teams. Knowing the correct ProdBOK term or life-cycle phase for a described situation is a recurring exam skill.

domains.name: Market Research and Competitive Analysis
domains.notes: Primary vs secondary research, qualitative vs quantitative methods, voice-of-customer, segmentation and targeting, and sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM). Competitive analysis frameworks (SWOT, Porter's Five Forces, competitive matrices) and positioning. Turning market and customer evidence into validated problems and opportunities. Choosing the appropriate research method or analysis for a described decision under time and budget constraints.

domains.name: Product Strategy and Business Planning
domains.notes: Product vision and strategy, the business case and business plan tailored to each major function, financial concepts a PM must defend (cost, margin, break-even, ROI, NPV at a conceptual level), and product/market data modeling. Portfolio thinking and build/buy/partner decisions. Aligning product strategy to corporate strategy and stakeholders. The exam tests whether a described initiative is justified and strategically aligned.

domains.name: Product Definition and Requirements
domains.notes: Translating validated needs into product specifications: market requirements (MRD) vs product requirements (PRD), functional vs non-functional requirements, use cases and personas, and prioritization of requirements. Managing scope and traceability from customer need to specification. Writing clear, testable requirements and choosing what to include in a first release. Distinguishing a good requirement from a poor one in a scenario.

domains.name: Roadmapping, Planning, and Cross-Functional Execution
domains.notes: Product roadmaps and release planning, project plans for each major activity, prioritization frameworks, and dependency and risk management across the front end of the life cycle. Coordinating engineering, design, marketing, sales, and support as the cross-functional 'go-to.' Stakeholder alignment and communication. Selecting the right prioritization or planning approach for a described constraint set.

domains.name: Go-to-Market, Launch, and Pricing
domains.notes: Product launch plans and readiness, launch tiers and channel/sales enablement, positioning and messaging, and the handoff from inbound to outbound. Pricing and packaging strategy (value-based, cost-plus, competitive; good-better-best), and the beachhead/whole-product view of a launch. Post-launch metrics and the maximize/retire phases at a PM level. Choosing the correct launch, pricing, or positioning move for a described market situation is the highest-value exam skill in this domain.

extra_guidance: AIPMM CPM is the vendor-neutral, globally recognized product management credential and the single best exam-format target in the PM space: it is a real ~2-hour, ~120-question proctored closed-book exam with a defined body of knowledge (the ProdBOK) and PROVEN Udemy exam-prep demand (existing CPM prep courses and a Coursera practice exam). CRITICAL accuracy note: AIPMM does NOT publish official per-domain percentage weightings or the passing score, so present the domain NAMES as the exam's objective areas but mark the weights as editorial estimates (leading '~'), never as AIPMM's official figures - state this where weights appear. Anchor EVERYTHING to the AIPMM ProdBOK vocabulary and the Seven-Phase Product Life Cycle (conceive, plan, develop, qualify, launch, maximize, retire) and phase-gate modeling, because the exam is terminology- and framework-driven: use AIPMM's exact terms (MRD, PRD, phase-gate, inbound/outbound, product/market data modeling) rather than generic PM slang. Practice questions MUST mix (a) crisp definition/term-matching questions and (b) short scenario questions with 'BEST / MOST appropriate / FIRST' framing where the PM must pick the right life-cycle phase, research method, prioritization approach, pricing model, or launch move. This course sits in an AI/tech certification catalog, so where natural, use modern SaaS/AI product examples (e.g. defining requirements for an ML feature, pricing an AI product, launching a data product) to keep it relevant - but keep the CORE anchored to AIPMM's framework, not AI theory. Frame the credential honestly as 'exam-focused preparation' - never promise a pass, guarantee, or 'first attempt' success (Udemy compliance). Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with time-management strategy for ~120 questions in ~2 hours plus guidance on ProdBOK-terminology elimination. Do NOT invent AIPMM's official passing score or exact fee; present the fee as approximate and advise verifying current AIPMM pricing. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor cloud terms (AWS/Azure/GCP) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
